assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Solar Industries India (consolidated, Rs crore), ORGANIC business only: the Omnia Holdings acquisition (signed 14-Sep-2026, completion expected early-to-mid 2027, subject to approvals) is NOT in the forecasts; its pro-forma effect is shown separately in the report. The company reports one segment, so the model is single-segment (revenue growth x EBITDA margin on Screener's basis); the revenue build by customer line (domestic explosives, international, defence, others) is in businessLines and the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Net profit in the engine includes minority interest (3.4% of FY26 profit); EPS divides by the share count implied by Screener (profit / EPS = 9.37 cr), which gives EPS attributable to Solar's shareholders at a constant minority share. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

businessLines._why: Bottom-up revenue by customer line (Rs crore). FY26 actuals from the Q4FY26 fact sheet. Sum = model revenue (checked by the authoring script).
businessLines._domesticWhy: FY27 +30%: management guided explosives (domestic + international) +30-33% with 10-15% from volume and 18-20% from price as ammonium-nitrate-linked prices rose; Q1 domestic +52% on a weak, monsoon-hit base (FY26 +3%, coal output 1,036 mt with CIL/SCCL down) and new Dhule/North India capacity. FY28 +10%: price falls back as inputs normalise, volumes grow ~8-10% (captive/commercial coal +10% in FY26, infra). FY29 +11%: Odisha and South India plants; MOFSL models ~15% CAGR FY26-30, we are lower in FY28-29.
businessLines._intlWhy: FY27 +32%: management 'around 30%' (price-aided); Q1 +65%. FY28 +18% and FY29 +15%: management's long-run 'around 10%' volume and 'around 15%' value growth plus new countries (Sierra Leone, Australia, Kazakhstan ramp). Excludes Omnia. MOFSL ~22% CAGR FY26-30.
businessLines._defenceWhy: FY27 Rs 4,500 cr = management's 'cross Rs 4,500 cr' (+71%); Q1 Rs 933 cr, the year is back-ended (FY26 Q4 was 38% of the year). FY28 +31% to Rs 5,900 cr and FY29 +25% to Rs 7,400 cr: the ~Rs 18,000 cr defence order book (Jun-26; ~Rs 11,000 cr international, ~Rs 6,000 cr Pinaka) covers FY28-29 if executed on schedule; we do not assume unannounced platform orders (Pinaka Mk2/guided, Bhargavastra, 155 mm). Street: PL ~Rs 6,200 cr FY28E; MOFSL Rs 6,070 cr FY28E and Rs 7,930 cr FY29E.
businessLines._othersWhy: Small (Rs 46-64 cr a year); held at Rs 50 cr.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business lines: FY27E Rs 13,940 cr (management target Rs 14,000 cr), FY28E Rs 16,685 cr (management's pre-Omnia FY28 indication: +17-20% to ~Rs 16,500 cr), FY29E Rs 19,600 cr. Defence rises from 27% of revenue (FY26) to 38% (FY29E).
assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (FY26 27.6%, Q1FY27 27.7%; the company's own 27.95%/27.91% includes other income). Management: 'maintain the current EBITDA margins' (May-2026), 'sustainable EBITDA margins in the 27-28% range' (AR FY26), 28-29% for FY27 on its basis (15-Sep call). Rising defence mix (higher-margin: Solar Defence and Aerospace earned a 30% pre-tax margin in FY26) is offset by price pass-through of ammonium-nitrate costs, which lifts revenue but not profit (pass-through covers ~60% of an increase). +20bp a year.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 Rs 2,050 cr = management guidance (FY26 Rs 1,556 cr, FY25 Rs 1,182 cr); ~Rs 450 cr spent in Q1. FY28-29 Rs 1,800 cr: the Rs 12,700 cr 10-year Maharashtra defence programme plus explosives plants (Odisha, Telangana/AP); PL assumes ~Rs 1,500 cr a year in FY28-29. Excludes the Omnia purchase.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 251 cr = 5.9% of average gross block (Rs 4,231 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs 80 cr (Rs 320 cr annualised). The engine adds all capex to gross block at once (CWIP Rs 731 cr held flat), so we use 5.6% to avoid charging a full year of depreciation on plants still being built.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applies only to net cash; Solar has net debt (Rs 867 cr at Mar-26 per the company), so treasury income is ~zero in the model.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Net of a recurring hyperinflation-accounting loss. The company books other income of Rs 128 cr in FY26 (incl. Rs 68 cr foreign-exchange gain, Rs 37 cr interest and Rs 20 cr investment gains) and a Rs 94.5 cr loss on subsidiaries in hyperinflationary economies (Turkey) inside other expenses (Rs 65 cr in FY25). Screener moves that loss out of operating profit and nets it against other income (FY26 Rs 33 cr, FY25 Rs 10 cr); our EBITDA margin is on that basis, so we hold net other income at Rs 35 cr a year.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (term loans, working-capital lines and leases; excludes Omnia acquisition debt)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs 134 cr on Rs 1,468 cr of debt; Q1FY27 Rs 41 cr (Rs 164 cr annualised). Debt rises with capex and working capital; Rs 170 / 180 / 180 cr. Omnia would add Rs 1,000-1,100 cr a year (management, Kotak).
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 26.6% (Rs 629 cr on Rs 2,365 cr); Q1FY27 26.9%. Mix of 25.2% India rate and overseas rates.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs 11/share ≈ 6% of attributable profit; 6-10% over FY23-26 as cash goes to capex.

dcf._betaWhy: Market-level risk: defence orders are lumpy and government-dependent, explosives follow coal and mining cycles, and debt is rising (Omnia would take it to ~1.5-2x EBITDA). Cost of equity 12.5%, used as the discount rate (net debt is small before Omnia).
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: defence and mining explosives can grow near India's nominal GDP for long, but defence budgets and export orders are cyclical.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~17% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15: domestic explosives at GDP-plus, defence growth slows as the order book matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: From ~28% towards 25%: competition in defence (private entrants such as Kalyani, state-owned Munitions India) and in explosives; the FY22-23 input spike took margins to ~19%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~9% of revenue (FY29E) to 6% as the defence build-out ends; FY24-26 averaged ~16%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Defence wins large new orders (Pinaka Mk2 or guided Pinaka, Bhargavastra after trials, 155 mm exports) and executes faster, taking defence to ~45% of sales by FY29; international grows 25%+ with new countries; margin rises toward 29% as defence mix lifts it.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Defence execution slips (trial delays, slower export orders, Pinaka deliveries spread out), FY27 revenue misses the Rs 14,000 cr target by ~6%, ammonium nitrate prices fall back and take explosives realisations with them, and margins drop toward 26% as new plants run below capacity.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Solar (PL 62x Sep-28E, Nuvama 55x Sep-28E, Jefferies 70x Sep-28E, ICICI Direct 70x FY28E, MOFSL 50x Dec-28E incl. Omnia). 50x = Solar's 46.5x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (no trough years), raised by the ~14% by which defence and explosives peers (BEL, HAL, BDL, Premier Explosives) traded above their five-year median P/E on 30-Sep-2026 (≈53x), less ~5% because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~27% a year) is below the 30-43% a year the history was earned on. Bull 54x (its 75th-percentile forward P/E since 2021), bear 30x (25th percentile).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net debt. 29x Sep-28E EBITDA = Solar's 43.4x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, raised by the same ~14% sector re-rating (≈49.5x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~64% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (≈30x), less the same ~5% growth discount.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 6%, less net debt.

cover.headline: India's explosives leader turned defence exporter: the growth is real, but the price already pays for it, and Omnia adds debt rather than value
cover.lead: Solar makes a quarter of India's commercial explosives, runs plants in 11 countries and has built, in a decade, a defence business that sold ₹2,634 cr in FY26 (from ₹249 cr in FY22): explosives for missiles, propellants, Pinaka rockets, ammunition and drones. Q1FY27 was excellent: revenue +70%, profit +89%, with defence +123%. Management targets ₹14,000 cr of revenue in FY27 (+42%) and ₹4,500 cr from defence. On 14-Sep-2026 it agreed to buy South Africa's Omnia for ₹12,951 cr in cash, which would double revenue at half the margin. The street values Solar on **P/E (50-70x FY28-Sep-28E EPS)**. We forecast organic EPS of ₹267 / ₹320 / ₹379 for FY27-29E, close to the street for FY27 and ~5-7% below PL for FY28-29. Applying **50x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹350** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹15,830, DCF ₹6,241. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Defence revenue grew ~80% a year over FY22-26 to 27% of sales; the defence order book is ~₹18,000 cr (Pinaka ~₹6,000 cr, exports ~₹11,000 cr). The defence subsidiary earned a 30% pre-tax margin in FY26, which is why group EBITDA margin rose from 19% (FY23) to 28%. We model defence at ₹{{as.businessLines.FY27E.defence|num}} / {{as.businessLines.FY28E.defence|num}} / {{as.businessLines.FY29E.defence|num}} cr.

arguments.h: But it is mostly exports, and the book has stopped growing
arguments.p: 60% of FY26 revenue was billed outside India; after international explosives that leaves ~₹2,000 cr, which we infer is mainly defence exports, ~75% of defence. The defence order book was ~₹18,000 cr in both Mar-26 and Jun-26: execution now runs ahead of new orders. Exports are lumpy and policy-exposed.

arguments.h: Explosives: steady volumes, inflated by price in FY27
arguments.p: Domestic explosives grew only 3% in FY26 as coal overburden removal fell; FY27's guided +30-33% for explosives is 18-20% price as ammonium nitrate costs are passed on. International grew 32% in FY26 and should grow ~30% in FY27 (Omnia excluded). Price pass-through lifts revenue, not profit: we hold EBITDA margin at {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}}-{{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Valuation: above its own history; Omnia does not change the math
arguments.p: At ₹19,700 Solar trades at 61.6x our FY28E EPS vs a 46.5x median forward P/E since 2021. Our 50x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}. Omnia, on a full year, would add ~₹420 cr of pre-tax profit (~10% of ours) for ~₹11,900 cr of net debt; at 6-10x EBITDA it is worth −₹170 to +₹590 a share to Solar.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): defence run-rate against the ₹4,500 cr target, working-capital release, margins as ammonium nitrate costs pass through.
Omnia: shareholder vote, competition and regulatory approvals and the final funding structure; completion expected early-to-mid 2027.
Defence orders: Pinaka follow-ons (Mk2, guided, replenishment), Bhargavastra counter-drone trials (management: complete in calendar 2026), 155 mm qualification, further export orders.
Ammonium nitrate prices and coal overburden removal after a weak FY26; the new Dhule, Odisha and South India plants.
Capex delivery (₹2,050 cr in FY27) and whether new capacity earns its cost while debt rises.

sections.title: Explosives for mines, and now rockets, shells and drones for armies

blocks.p: Solar Industries makes the explosives that break rock in coal, iron-ore and limestone mines, quarries and tunnels, and the detonators and cords that set them off ("initiating systems"). It sells **bulk explosives** (emulsions pumped into blast holes at the mine, often from trucks), **packaged explosives** (cartridges; management calls Solar the world's largest maker) and **initiating systems**. Since about 2010 it has added **defence**: high-energy materials (HMX, RDX, TNT), propellants for the Akash, Pinaka and BrahMos missiles, complete Pinaka rockets, warheads, 23-155 mm ammunition, Nagastra loitering munitions (drones that dive onto a target) and the Bhargavastra counter-drone system now in trials. The company reports one segment; its fact sheets split revenue by customer.

sections.title: Two industries: a slow-growing, price-led explosives market and a fast-growing defence market

blocks.p: India produced about 2.3 million tonnes of commercial explosives in FY25, up from 1.5 million in FY20 (~9% a year, PESO data via MOFSL). Mining, mostly coal, takes a substantial share (AR FY26); the rest goes to quarries, roads, tunnels and dams. Demand follows overburden removal (the rock stripped to reach coal) more than coal output itself. FY26 was weak: coal output was "quite muted" at 1,036 mt as heavy rain cut Coal India and Singareni production, though captive and commercial mines grew 10%. Explosives are sold largely by tender, so suppliers compete on cost, and ammonium nitrate (the main input) is passed on with a lag.

Defence is a different market. India's defence capital spending is expected to grow ~16% a year for four years and private companies' share of listed defence revenue rose from 9% to 16% over FY23-26 (Jefferies). Abroad, wars in Europe and West Asia have created a shortage of artillery shells, rockets and explosives, with demand visibility of 5-7 years (AR FY26). Solar sits at the intersection: it makes the energetic materials every munition needs and is integrating up into complete rockets and drones.

sections.title: Omnia: a large, cheap, low-margin business bought with debt; roughly value-neutral at the price paid

blocks.p: On 14-Sep-2026 Solar agreed to buy 100% of Johannesburg-listed Omnia Holdings for ZAR 134.5 a share in cash: about US$1.355 bn or ₹12,951 cr, Solar's largest deal by far. Founded 1953, Johannesburg; 23 countries, 70+ distribution centres, 3,500+ employees. FY26 (Mar) revenue ZAR 24.2 bn (~US$1.41 bn, ₹13,307 cr): agriculture 54%, mining (BME: bulk and packaged explosives, AXXIS electronic detonators, blasting services) 41%, chemicals (Protea) 5%. Segment EBITDA ZAR 2.98 bn (agri 1.66, mining 1.31, chemicals 0.01); net cash ~US$110 mn. Owns nitric acid / ammonium nitrate plants (largest in the region). Completion needs Omnia shareholders, competition and other regulators, and is expected in early-to-mid 2027. Solar's stock fell ~17% in two days. We keep Omnia **out of our forecasts and target** until it closes and the funding is fixed, as PL and Goldman Sachs do (MOFSL includes it), and show its effect here.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Solar has a real but narrow moat. In explosives it is the scale, low-cost, licensed incumbent close to the mines, which wins tenders and share, but tender buyers set the price and ammonium nitrate is bought in. In defence it has a genuine capability lead among Indian private firms (integrated from energetic materials to complete rockets), which is why defence margins are higher; but that lead is being contested by well-funded groups, it depends on government trials and export licences, and it is young. The premium the market pays assumes the defence lead converts into a decade of large orders. That is possible, not proven.

sections.title: Ten years of 21% growth, with one input-cost boom and bust and a defence-led margin step-up

blocks.p: Solar's revenue grew from ₹1,449 cr in FY16 to ₹9,838 cr in FY26, about 21% a year, and net profit from ₹178 cr to ₹1,737 cr, about 26% a year. The path had three phases. Until FY21 it was a pure explosives company (exports and overseas already ~35-42% of sales) growing ~12% a year with a ~20% EBITDA margin. In FY22-23 the ammonium nitrate (AN) price spike after the Russia-Ukraine war pushed revenue up 57% and 75% (prices are passed on), while the margin slipped to ~19%; when AN fell, FY24 revenue dropped 12%. Since FY24 defence has changed the mix: defence rose from 9% of revenue in FY24 to 27% in FY26, and EBITDA margin rose from 19% in FY23 to 28% in FY26.

sections.title: Earnings quality: profits are real, but cash lagged badly in FY26 and the definitions need care

bullets: **Cash lagged profit in FY26.** Operating cash flow was 36% of net profit in FY26 (₹621 cr vs ₹1,737 cr), after 192% in FY25 and 161% in FY24. Over FY15-26 operating cash (₹7,290 cr) slightly exceeded profit (₹6,773 cr). The FY26 gap is inventory (₹1,742 cr vs ₹1,040 cr) and receivables (₹1,858 cr vs ₹1,239 cr); management says the inventory build was deliberate.

**A recurring "below-the-line" loss.** Turkey is accounted for as a hyperinflationary economy; the restatement cost ₹94.5 cr in FY26 and ₹65 cr in FY25 (in other expenses). Other income of ₹128 cr includes a ₹68 cr foreign-exchange gain. Screener moves the Turkish loss out of operating profit, so its EBITDA margin (27.6%) is a little flattering; the company's own EBITDA (₹2,750 cr) includes other income.

**Minority interest.** ₹59 cr in FY26 (3.4% of profit) and ₹78 cr in FY25; EPS uses attributable profit (₹1,678 cr). Our model carries profit including minorities and divides by Screener's implied share count (9.4 cr), which keeps EPS on an attributable basis.

**Estimates in revenue.** The auditors' key audit matters are the "powder factor" provision (₹37 cr: a deduction from sales based on blast output achieved at customer sites, settled later) and the Level-3 fair value of ₹135 cr of unlisted equity and preference-share investments.
**Currency.** A weaker rupee lifted reported profit (export receivables) and added ₹276 cr of translation gains to equity in FY26; the reverse can happen.

**Disclosure gaps.** One reported segment, no EBITDA by line, no split of defence between India and exports, no Q1FY27 call. Investors are asked to trust a defence story they can only see in aggregate.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Audits are clean (S R B C & Co jointly with Gandhi Rathi & Co) and profits are cash-backed over time. The flag is for FY26's weak cash conversion, a recurring hyperinflation charge outside "EBITDA", and thin disclosure on the defence business that carries the valuation.

The swing came from working capital: inventory days rose from 95 to 130 and receivable days from 60 to 69. Management says the inventory was built on purpose "to mitigate the risk arising from geopolitical uncertainties" and should normalise "maybe in the next 2 quarters". Our model holds working capital at FY26's share of revenue, which is conservative if that happens.

Rising defence mix (higher-margin: Solar Defence and Aerospace earned a 30% pre-tax margin in FY26) is offset by price pass-through of ammonium-nitrate costs, which lifts revenue but not profit (pass-through covers ~60% of an increase). +20bp a year.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 Rs 2,050 cr = management guidance (FY26 Rs 1,556 cr, FY25 Rs 1,182 cr); ~Rs 450 cr spent in Q1. FY28-29 Rs 1,800 cr: the Rs 12,700 cr 10-year Maharashtra defence programme plus explosives plants (Odisha, Telangana/AP); PL assumes ~Rs 1,500 cr a year in FY28-29. Excludes the Omnia purchase.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 251 cr = 5.9% of average gross block (Rs 4,231 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs 80 cr (Rs 320 cr annualised). The engine adds all capex to gross block at once (CWIP Rs 731 cr held flat), so we use 5.6% to avoid charging a full year of depreciation on plants still being built.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applies only to net cash; Solar has net debt (Rs 867 cr at Mar-26 per the company), so treasury income is ~zero in the model.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Net of a recurring hyperinflation-accounting loss. The company books other income of Rs 128 cr in FY26 (incl. Rs 68 cr foreign-exchange gain, Rs 37 cr interest and Rs 20 cr investment gains) and a Rs 94.5 cr loss on subsidiaries in hyperinflationary economies (Turkey) inside other expenses (Rs 65 cr in FY25). Screener moves that loss out of operating profit and nets it against other income (FY26 Rs 33 cr, FY25 Rs 10 cr); our EBITDA margin is on that basis, so we hold net other income at Rs 35 cr a year.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (term loans, working-capital lines and leases; excludes Omnia acquisition debt)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs 134 cr on Rs 1,468 cr of debt; Q1FY27 Rs 41 cr (Rs 164 cr annualised). Debt rises with capex and working capital; Rs 170 / 180 / 180 cr. Omnia would add Rs 1,000-1,100 cr a year (management, Kotak).
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 26.6% (Rs 629 cr on Rs 2,365 cr); Q1FY27 26.9%. Mix of 25.2% India rate and overseas rates.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs 11/share ≈ 6% of attributable profit; 6-10% over FY23-26 as cash goes to capex.

dcf._betaWhy: Market-level risk: defence orders are lumpy and government-dependent, explosives follow coal and mining cycles, and debt is rising (Omnia would take it to ~1.5-2x EBITDA). Cost of equity 12.5%, used as the discount rate (net debt is small before Omnia).
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: defence and mining explosives can grow near India's nominal GDP for long, but defence budgets and export orders are cyclical.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~17% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15: domestic explosives at GDP-plus, defence growth slows as the order book matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: From ~28% towards 25%: competition in defence (private entrants such as Kalyani, state-owned Munitions India) and in explosives; the FY22-23 input spike took margins to ~19%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~9% of revenue (FY29E) to 6% as the defence build-out ends; FY24-26 averaged ~16%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Defence wins large new orders (Pinaka Mk2 or guided Pinaka, Bhargavastra after trials, 155 mm exports) and executes faster, taking defence to ~45% of sales by FY29; international grows 25%+ with new countries; margin rises toward 29% as defence mix lifts it.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Defence execution slips (trial delays, slower export orders, Pinaka deliveries spread out), FY27 revenue misses the Rs 14,000 cr target by ~6%, ammonium nitrate prices fall back and take explosives realisations with them, and margins drop toward 26% as new plants run below capacity.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Solar (PL 62x Sep-28E, Nuvama 55x Sep-28E, Jefferies 70x Sep-28E, ICICI Direct 70x FY28E, MOFSL 50x Dec-28E incl. Omnia). 50x = Solar's 46.5x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (no trough years), raised by the ~14% by which defence and explosives peers (BEL, HAL, BDL, Premier Explosives) traded above their five-year median P/E on 30-Sep-2026 (≈53x), less ~5% because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~27% a year) is below the 30-43% a year the history was earned on. Bull 54x (its 75th-percentile forward P/E since 2021), bear 30x (25th percentile).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
